item.title: [PBV7-489] Add Grafana diagnostics and validate production readiness
item.description:
Source and parent

Specification: Realtime WebSocket Platform – .NET 10, Redis, and Kubernetes
Parent Epic: PBV7-484

Context

Provide operators with a version-controlled Grafana dashboard, actionable alerts, diagnostic links, capacity evidence, CI/CD controls, and runbooks sufficient to identify and recover from application and infrastructure problems.

Requirements

  • Export Prometheus-compatible application metrics for connection, protocol, queue, handler, security, Redis, drain, and error behavior.
  • Integrate available Kubernetes, Traefik, MetalLB, certificate, and Redis metrics.
  • Create a Grafana dashboard as version-controlled JSON and provision it automatically through the approved Grafana or Helm mechanism.
  • Provide environment, namespace, cluster/instance, and pod variables; do not expose unrestricted tenant variables or introduce tenant-level high-cardinality labels.
  • Add service-overview panels for availability, readiness, active/peak connections, opens, closes, reconnects, throughput, and replica distribution.
  • Add connection-diagnostic panels for handshakes, authentication/authorization/origin failures, close codes, connection duration, heartbeat timeout, and abnormal disconnects.
  • Add message panels for handler latency, invalid/rejected messages, outbound queue depth, backpressure, dropped messages, and slow-consumer disconnects.
  • Add Redis panels for connection state, reconnects, errors, latency, resource usage, replication, persistence, failover, and Streams lag/pending/acknowledgment/recovery where enabled.
  • Add Kubernetes and edge panels for CPU, memory, throttling, restarts, readiness, Traefik upgrades and 4xx/5xx responses, MetalLB health/advertisement, certificates, and rollout state.
  • Link panels to relevant logs, traces, pod views, and runbook sections.
  • Add alert rules for service unavailability, abnormal reconnects, authentication failure spikes, queue saturation, dropped messages, Redis disconnect or latency, replica loss, excessive restarts, certificate problems, ingress errors, VIP advertisement loss, and rollout failure.
  • Add dashboards and alert validation to CI or deployment verification where practical.
  • Implement connection, fan-out, burst, large-message, slow-client, and soak tests.
  • Establish measured capacity and scaling thresholds; define HPA inputs using connections, queue depth, CPU, and memory as appropriate.
  • Add independent build, test, AOT publish, Helm validation, vulnerability scan, SBOM, immutable publish, staging promotion, and rollback controls.
  • Publish deployment, operations, alert response, troubleshooting, Redis recovery, certificate, Traefik, MetalLB, scaling, and rollback runbooks.

Dependencies

  • Instrumented gateway and Redis integration.
  • Deployed Kubernetes, Traefik, MetalLB, Prometheus-compatible metrics, log, trace, and Grafana platforms.
  • Approved staging environment for load and failure testing.

Completion criteria

  • The dashboard is provisioned from source control with no required manual panel creation.
  • All required application, Redis, Kubernetes, Traefik, and MetalLB diagnostic areas contain data or clearly document unavailable metrics.
  • Alerts are routed through the approved notification path and link to actionable runbooks.
  • Measured load and soak results define supported capacity, resource settings, and scaling thresholds.
  • CI/CD promotes the same immutable artifact between environments and provides a tested rollback.
  • Operations, troubleshooting, recovery, and dashboard documentation completes technical review.

Testing criteria

  • Generate controlled normal traffic and verify every primary dashboard row and variable.
  • Inject authentication and Origin failures and verify panels and alerts identify them.
  • Saturate an outbound queue and simulate a slow client; verify queue, backpressure, dropped-message, and close-code diagnostics.
  • Interrupt Redis and introduce latency; verify connection, reconnect, latency, error, and Streams panels and alerts.
  • Delete gateway pods, restart Traefik, drain a node, and exercise a rolling deployment; verify Kubernetes, ingress, reconnect, and rollout diagnostics.
  • Exercise MetalLB speaker/controller or advertisement failure in an approved test environment and verify detection.
  • Test certificate-expiry or invalid-certificate alert logic without disrupting production.
  • Run connection, fan-out, burst, permitted-large-message, slow-client, and soak tests and record results.
  • Test alert delivery, dashboard links, log/trace correlation, and each referenced runbook.
  • Rehearse deployment rollback and recovery from a failed release.
item.summary: Add Grafana diagnostics and validate production readiness
